settings.introHTML: This lesson teaches you how to talk about free-time activities in French. You will practise using verbs such as faire and jouer to describe hobbies, sports, music, and weekend routines, while learning how French uses partitive articles with these activities. The unit also helps you notice adjective agreement and improve pronunciation of common -tion words.
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Talk about hobbies, sports, and weekend routines in French.
  • Use faire with the correct partitive article (du, de la, de l', des).
  • Use jouer de for musical instruments and jouer à for sports and games.
  • Recognise and apply adjective agreement patterns such as sportif / sportive.
  • Pronounce common French words ending in -tion more confidently.

dialogues.instructionsTextHTML: This section introduces short dialogues about hobbies, weekend plans, musical instruments, and sports in French.

dialogues1.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Je n'aime pas du tout l'escalade. C'est trop dangereux ! Je préfère l'équitation. J'adore les chevaux !
I don't like climbing at all. It's too dangerous! I prefer horse riding. I love horses!

dialogues2.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Qu'est-ce que tu fais le weekend ?
What do you do at the weekend?
Le samedi, je fais de l'aviron. Je prends mon petit-déjeuner au café avec mes amis. Je vais en ville pour faire du shopping. Le soir, je sors avec ma copine.
On Saturdays, I go rowing. I have my breakfast in a café with my friends. I go into town to do some shopping. In the evening, I go out with my girlfriend.
Le dimanche, je fais de la natation. L'après-midi, s'il fait beau, je fais de la randonnée avec mon frère. S'il fait mauvais, je lis un peu ou je regarde la télé. Et toi ?
On Sundays, I go swimming. In the afternoon, if the weather's good, I go hiking with my brother. If the weather's bad, I read a bit, or I watch television. What about you?
Je ne fais pas grand-chose. Je fais la grasse matinée. Je vois mes amis. Quelquefois, je vais au cinéma ou je vais en boîte. Ça dépend !
I don't do much. I have a lie-in. I see my friends. Sometimes I go to the cinema, or I go clubbing. It depends.

dialogues3.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Vous jouez d'un instrument de musique ?
Do you play a musical instrument?
Oui, je joue du piano et de la clarinette aussi. Et vous ?
Yes, I play the piano and the clarinet. What about you?
Je joue de l'accordéon et je joue du piano aussi.
I play the accordion, and I play the piano too.

dialogues4.informationTextHTML: Read each phrase, then play its audio clip to check pronunciation and meaning.
phrases: Le samedi, je joue au basket. Ça te dit de jouer au basket avec nous ?
On Saturdays, I play basketball. Do you fancy playing basketball with us?
Le samedi, je ne peux pas - je joue au volley. C'est dommage !
On Saturdays, I can't - I play volleyball. It's a pity!

vocabulary.instructionsTextHTML: This section introduces key free-time vocabulary used throughout the unit.
vocabulary.informationTextHTML:
You will learn:

  • Core vocabulary for hobbies and free time (for example temps libre, loisirs, passe-temps).
  • Useful verbs for activities and games (for example faire, jouer à, jouer de).
  • Sports and leisure nouns (for example aviron, escalade, natation, pétanque).
  • Useful adjectives for describing preferences and activities (for example actif / active, dangereux / dangereuse, sportif / sportive).

grammar1.informationTextHTML: This section explains how adjectives such as sportif change in the feminine form.

grammar2.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the verb faire and the partitive articles used with many leisure activities.

grammar3.informationTextHTML: This section explains the difference between jouer de for instruments and jouer à for sports and games.

grammar4.informationTextHTML: This section highlights some useful noun-ending patterns that can help you predict grammatical gender.

pronunciation1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on how French words ending in -tion are pronounced. Listen carefully and repeat each example aloud.

pronunciation2.informationTextHTML: Here, extend the same pronunciation pattern to more familiar words. Listen, compare, and repeat.

memoryMatchGame1.informationTextHTML: Match each picture to the correct French word. You can also listen to the French word cards for help. Use Show answer to reveal the matched pairs, and Reset to start a new round.

inlineChoiceGroup1.instructionsText: Choose the correct partitive article or instrument form.
inlineChoiceGroup1.informationTextHTML: Read each sentence and choose the correct form to complete it. Work through all items first, then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Show answers to reveal the correct forms, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Je fais [*du|de la|de l'|des] shopping.
Vous faites [*du|de la|*de l'|des] jogging le matin ?
Tu fais [du|de la|*de l'|des] aviron ?
J'aime faire [*du|de la|de l'|des] lèche-vitrine.
Ma sœur aime faire [du|*de la|de l'|des] peinture.
Je fais [du|de la|*de l'|des] équitation pendant mon temps libre.
Je joue [du|*de la|de l'|des] batterie.
Tu joues [du|*de la|de l'|des] guitare ?
Mes parents jouent [*du|de la|de l'|des] piano.
Vous jouez [*du|de la|de l'|des] trombone ?

inlineChoiceGroup2.instructionsText: Choose au, à la, à l', or aux as appropriate.
inlineChoiceGroup2.informationTextHTML: Read each sentence and choose the correct contracted form after jouer à. Work through all items first, then use Check answers to review your choices. If needed, use Show answers to reveal the correct forms, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Le lundi, il joue [*au|à la|à l'|aux] foot.
Le mardi, il joue [*au|à la|à l'|aux] tennis.
Le mercredi, il joue [*au|à la|à l'|aux] volley.
Le jeudi, il joue [au|*à la|à l'|aux] pétanque.
Le vendredi, il joue [au|à la|à l'|*aux] boules.
Le samedi, il joue [*au|à la|à l'|aux] baseball. Le soir, il joue [*au|à la|à l'|aux] babyfoot avec ses amis.
Le dimanche, il est un peu fatigué. Il reste à la maison. Quelquefois, il joue [au|à la|à l'|*aux] échecs avec son frère.
